Hernĭci , ōrum, m. herna = saxum in the Sabine and Marscar lang.,
I.an Italian people in Latium, between the Æqui and Volsci, Liv. 2, 22; 40 sq.; cf.: Hernici dicti a saxis, quae Marsi herna dicunt, Paul. ex Fest. p. 100 Müll.—
II. Deriv.: Hernĭ-cus , a, um, adj., of or belonging to the Hernici, Hernician: “ager,” Plin. 3, 5, 9, § 63 : “terra,” Ov. F. 3, 90 : “saxa,” Verg. A. 7, 684 ; Sil. 4, 226; 8, 393; cf. Stat. S. 4, 5, 56.
Subst.: Hernĭcus , i, m., the Hernician, collect., Juv. 14, 180.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
